protocol.transparent_baseline: exact embedding cosine plus 0.075 times exact structured match count inside the embedding candidate set
protocol.learned_baseline: 12-epoch pairwise-logistic linear ranker over exact embedding cosine and normalized exact structured match count
protocol.hdc_method: the same pairwise ranker with normalized Hamming similarity from an 8000-dimensional packed-bipolar structural bundle
protocol.labels: original WANDS human relevance judgments; unjudged candidate pairs are treated as gain zero

limitations: The learned baseline is a small deterministic pairwise linear ranker, not a cross-encoder or production learning-to-rank model.
The compositional slice has only 93 holdout queries and only 13 queries state more than one extracted attribute beyond class.
The workload tests explicit product attributes and category-derived graph answers, not inferred relations or contradictory evidence.
Packed-HDC feature timing is reported separately from candidate generation and final linear scoring.
A second external compositional or relational domain is still required by the graduation rule.
conclusion: Candidate-local packed-bipolar HDC does not improve the learned reranker. It is significantly worse on NDCG@10 at 50 and 100 candidates, has no significant advantage at 200 candidates, and reduces graph-answer top-1 by one holdout query. The transparent hybrid path remains simpler, while the learned non-HDC reranker is significantly better than fixed fusion at 200 candidates. The evidence strengthens the no-go decision for HDC and supports investing in hybrid candidate generation and reranking.
